findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the primary is actually instructed to SKIP validating seeded/credited criteria (e.g., annotate or omit the criterion PROSE, or add an explicit 'already credited — do not re-verify' directive co-located with the criteria list), not merely omit ids from the data-only manifest; state where that instruction lives relative to the criteria prose.
evidence: Plan: "primary_criteria_manifest (completion_recovery.py:540) omits already-banked ids, so the primary run (launched first, :495) is instructed only on unproven criteria — 'spend budget only on unproven criteria' holds on the PRIMARY run"

primary_criteria_manifest docstring: 'appends a volatile DATA-ONLY id manifest ... to the primary's untrusted ticket context; the authoritative banking instructions remain in the system prompt' — the criteria are still listed as prose in the base context; the manifest only supplies ids

Instruction-locality: the decision rule 'skip criteria already credited by seed' is not co-located with where the primary is shown the criteria; omitting ids does not remove/annotate the prose criteria the model is asked to verify
findings.finding: The plan claims 'spend budget only on unproven criteria holds on the PRIMARY run' by having primary_criteria_manifest omit seeded ids, but that manifest is a DATA-ONLY id list; the base verifier context still lists every acceptance criterion as prose, so omitting an id does not instruct the model to SKIP validating that criterion. The mechanism does not clearly produce the claimed 'validate only unproven' behavior on the primary.
findings.location: Plan step 3 ('Seeded ids are EXCLUDED from the primary's work surface... primary run is instructed only on unproven criteria'); primary_criteria_manifest, src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_banking.py:193-211
scenarios: A re-verify seeds several PASS criteria; the primary receives a manifest missing those ids but still sees all criteria in prose and re-validates them, defeating the intended budget savings — the exact 'exhaustion then converges across runs' benefit the plan promises may not materialize on the primary.
findings.suggested_fix: In the primary context, render seeded criteria with an explicit 'ALREADY CREDITED — do not re-verify; spend no budget' annotation adjacent to the criterion text (or drop those criteria from the primary's prose criteria list entirely), rather than relying on id-omission from the DATA-ONLY manifest alone; add a test asserting the primary prose/context marks or omits seeded criteria, not just the id manifest.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify fingerprint behavior for a multi-level epic whose DIRECT children have empty file_impact (grandchildren carry the paths): either recurse the child file_impact union to the first non-empty descendant frontier, or treat an empty direct-child union as 'fingerprint unresolvable' and fail-open to re-verification (never a constant/empty fingerprint that skips invalidation).
evidence: Plan: 'when own file_impact is empty but the ticket has children ... the fingerprint is the union of direct-child file_impact blobs ... NOT _subtree_impacts'
Plan: 'Whole-tree sha is the fallback ONLY for childless tickets with empty file_impact.'
_subtree_impacts (completion_prefetch.py:257) is precisely the whole-subtree BFS the plan rejects; direct-children-only means grandchild file_impact is unseen
Fail-open discipline elsewhere is 'never stale credit' — this branch violates that intent for multi-level epics
findings.finding: The epic-case scoped fingerprint (union of DIRECT-child file_impact blobs) does not invalidate on code edits for a multi-level epic whose direct children have empty file_impact and whose grandchildren carry the real paths: the direct-child union is empty, yet the whole-tree-sha fallback is scoped 'ONLY for childless tickets with empty file_impact' — an epic-of-epics HAS children, so it misses both, producing a constant/empty fingerprint that grants stale cached-PASS credit after grandchild code changes.
findings.location: Plan step 3 (scoped fingerprint / epic case); AC line 3
scenarios: An epic whose direct children are themselves epics/sub-epics with empty own file_impact; the real file paths live on grandchildren
A grandchild's source file is edited between verify runs — blob sha would change but the epic's fingerprint (empty union) does not, so the cached PASS is wrongly credited
findings.suggested_fix: When the direct-child file_impact union is empty but children exist, fall through to fail-open (disable reuse for that run) rather than the childless whole-tree fallback — mirroring the git-failure fail-open path so no cached PASS is ever credited on an empty fingerprint.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether lever 1 (budget raise) alone resolves the observed false-unmets, and justify lever 3's incremental value/complexity — or split the cross-run cache into its own ticket with a measured latency target.

Design intent frames the budget's ONLY goal as runaway prevention, which lever 1 directly serves; lever 3 targets re-verify latency, a separate axis

The cache introduces a new store at .rebar/cache/completion_verdicts/, a net-new scoped-fingerprint helper, seeded-flag plumbing through CriterionBank.for_run/primary_criteria_manifest, and a scoped change to merge_finalizer_with_bank — a multi-surface addition
completion_banking.py:401 confirms CriterionBank is deliberately run-scoped; the new store is genuinely additive, not a reuse
findings.finding: Lever 3 (the cross-run PASS-verdict cache — a new ticket-scoped store, a net-new blob-sha fingerprint helper, and a finalizer-scoping change) is a substantial new subsystem stacked on lever 1 (the budget raise). The plan motivates it by defect (3) (re-verify cost ~10 min/cycle) but does not state whether lever 1 alone resolves the observed false-unmets (fb8a: 2; pony: 5-then-1), leaving lever 3's incremental value unquantified against its complexity. The plan already did strong NIH diligence on the fingerprint helper (correctly ruling out material_fingerprint and _subtree_impacts), so this is a scope-sequencing coach, not a rebuild finding.
findings.location: Plan section 'Plan' item 3 (cross-run PASS-verdict cache); AC line 3
scenarios: If lever 1's raised budget alone eliminates the false-unmets, lever 3 could ship as a separate follow-up ticket with its own value measurement rather than coupling a large store+finalizer change into this budget fix

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define a RETIRE/cleanup path for the completion_verdicts cache (e.g. overwrite/delete the stale entry on fingerprint mismatch, or a bounded per-ticket cap / prune-on-close), and add a test asserting invalidated entries are not left to accumulate.
evidence: 'Cache at .rebar/cache/completion_verdicts/<ticket>/<criterion-hash>.json, written ONLY on a validated PASS at finalize'
No mention of eviction, TTL, pruning, or cleanup of stale/invalidated entries anywhere in step 3 or the ACs
T9: 'is there a RETIRE/cleanup path, or does it leak/accumulate? ... shared state with no ... retirement path = MAJOR'
findings.finding: The new persistent ticket-scoped verdict cache at .rebar/cache/completion_verdicts/<ticket>/<criterion-hash>.json has a defined CREATE/UPDATE/CONSUME path but NO RETIRE/cleanup path — entries accumulate one file per (ticket, criterion-hash) and are never pruned. On fingerprint/text invalidation the plan re-verifies (fail-open) but the stale on-disk file is never deleted, so cache files leak and accumulate across tickets and edits indefinitely.
scenarios: A criterion's file_impact is edited repeatedly across many re-verify cycles, leaving one stale invalidated JSON per fingerprint generation that is never removed
Long-lived repos accumulate verdict files for closed/deleted tickets
findings.suggested_fix: On a fingerprint/text mismatch at seed time, delete (or overwrite) the stale <criterion-hash>.json rather than only falling open to re-verification; optionally prune the <ticket>/ directory when the ticket closes.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Instrument the cache path: log (at least) seeded-credit ids applied at run start and the git-fingerprint-failure fail-open branch, so operators can see cache hits/misses and reuse-disabled events.
evidence: 'a git failure disables reuse for that run (fail-open to re-verification, never stale credit)' — no stated log/metric on this branch
'still-valid entries are SEEDED into the run's CriterionBank' — no stated observability of which ids were credited from cache
T5b: 'New failure points instrumented with a metric/log/trace/alert.'
findings.finding: The plan adds new failure/degradation points (git rev-parse failure -> fail-open re-verify; a seeded PASS crediting a criterion the primary run never re-examines) but does not instrument them. There is no log/metric/trace when a seeded credit is applied, when a fingerprint git call fails and disables reuse, or on a cache hit vs miss — leaving operators unable to see WHY a re-verify credited a criterion or silently re-proved everything.
findings.location: Plan step 3 (scoped fingerprint / seeding) and step 4
scenarios: A silent git failure disables all reuse, operators see full re-verification with no signal explaining it
A stale-looking credit is questioned and there is no audit trail of which criteria were seeded from the persistent cache
findings.suggested_fix: Emit a structured log line on (a) each seeded criterion credited and (b) fingerprint-resolution failure that disabled reuse for the run.
